name: Semantic Isolation of Constraints
description: Instead of providing explicit algebraic formulas (like `p1+p2 > T` or `sum(p_c) > T`), the certificates are defined by semantically isolating the scheduling constraints they violate ("even if it were the only job" and "even if the other stage took zero time"). This forces the model to deduce the mathematical conditions from physical mechanics rather than pattern-matching explicit inequalities.
